title: Security
description: Review of secure boot, debug access, keys and credentials, input handling, vulnerability management, and privacy.

items.text: Debug ports (SWD/JTAG) are locked or disabled on production units
items.hint: Set read-out protection or debug authentication as a production step, and verify it at end of line.

items.text: Only signed firmware can boot, or the decision not to is documented
items.hint: Secure boot with a root of trust in ROM or locked flash.

items.text: Anti-rollback prevents installing an older, vulnerable image
items.hint: A monotonic security version in OTP or protected storage.

items.text: Bootloader and option-byte protection can't be undone without erasing secrets
items.hint: Check what an attacker can do with the regression from RDP level 1 to level 0.

items.text: No secrets (keys, passwords, API tokens) are in the source code or the image
items.hint: Search the repository history too. Shared secrets across all devices are a single point of failure.

items.text: Each device has unique credentials, provisioned in production
items.hint: Per-device certificates or keys, injected in a controlled step and recorded.

items.text: Keys are stored in protected storage (secure element, TrustZone, encrypted flash)
items.hint: Not in plain external flash that can be read with a clip.

items.text: User credentials (Wi-Fi passwords, accounts) are encrypted at rest and never logged
items.hint: Check debug logs, crash dumps, and support bundles.

items.text: There is a plan for revoking and rotating keys
items.hint: What happens when one device's key leaks? When the signing key leaks?

items.text: All external input is validated for length and range before use
items.hint: Network, BLE, USB, serial, files, and sensor data. No unchecked memcpy from a packet.

items.text: Banned functions (strcpy, sprintf, gets) are not used, or are flagged by the build
items.hint: Use bounded versions and enforce it with a linter rule.

items.text: Parsers for external data are fuzzed
items.hint: Even a short fuzzing run off target finds most buffer bugs in a parser.

items.text: Stack protection, and other compiler and linker hardening, are enabled
items.hint: -fstack-protector-strong, and the MPU marking RAM non-executable.

items.text: Third-party components are checked against known vulnerabilities (CVEs)
items.hint: Use the SBOM. Repeat at each release and on a schedule after launch.

items.text: The applicable cybersecurity rules for the target markets are identified
items.hint: E.g. EN 18031 for radio products in the EU (RED), the Cyber Resilience Act, ETSI EN 303 645, the US Cyber Trust Mark.

items.text: There is a vulnerability disclosure contact and a patch process
items.hint: Required by several of the rules above. Agree who owns it with the client.

items.text: A threat model lists assets, attackers, and mitigations
items.hint: Even a one-page STRIDE table focuses the security review.

items.text: Personal data collected by the device is listed, minimized, and disclosed
items.hint: Location, schedules, usage patterns. Check the privacy policy matches what the firmware sends.
